QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_54

question.text: Under SAS-1100 a 'housing unit delivered' output is simple; the OUTCOME indicator is:

answer.text: Improved quality of life and access to basic facilities (safe water, toilets, feeling safe, disaster capacity) plus reduced annual repair expense (the Niwas case cites Rs 10,000 saved per family)

explanation.text: The Logic: Outcome captures the CHANGE in well-being — improved quality of life, safe water and toilets, feeling safe, disaster capacity, and reduced repair expenses. The Niwas case explicitly cites a Rs 10,000 annual saving per family. The Trap: Options A, B and D describe output, aesthetic or specification indicators rather than outcomes. Note: Distinguish outputs (units delivered) from outcomes (changes in well-being and household expense). Use the Niwas Rs 10,000/year repair-expense saving as a concrete outcome example.
